body:
Pasting my analysis here, for tracking (discussing it inside https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/bugsquad?msg=FzHLD3W5gFvj77n5o chat channel since someone might already be solving this) :


> The problematic behavior appears to originate in `Window::_window_input()` and is **focus-related rather than **just** event-type-related**.
> 
> In normal conditions, **mouse button, mouse motion, and mouse wheel events are all correctly blocked** when a detached popup window has an exclusive child (`exclusive_child != nullptr`).
> However, when a **drag operation starts on the popup**, the popup gains focus. From that point onward, **mouse motion continues to be forwarded** to the underlying inspector, even though the exclusive child is still active.
> 
> This results in the inspector reacting to drags (scrolling, resizing, etc.) while interacting with a detached popup.
> 
> Relevant code path https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/757bba192ef4c3254b44bc0d2c8cf36aa3343e30/scene/main/window.cpp#L1825 :
> 
> ```cpp
> //...
> 	if (*exclusive_child != nullptr*) {
>                 ... //will properly go here when clicking outside then moving
> 		if (!is_embedding_subwindows()) {
> 			return;
> 		}
> 	}
> // Drag plus motion will go here, which pushes the input
> ```
> 
> From what I can tell, **input blocking works correctly until focus is acquired via a drag**. Once focused, mouse motion continues through `_input_from_window()` and `push_input()`, which allows the inspector behind the popup to react.
@akien-mga after more testing https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111113 doesn't fix this issue. Sorry!
